# Data Safety and UX Requirements Checklist: Todo 中心の統合メモサイドバー

**Purpose**: Markdown 保存・競合保護と、統合サイドバー・ライブ編集・アクセシビリティの要件品質を、実装前 PR レビューの正式ゲートとして評価する。
**Created**: 2026-09-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness — Markdown Storage and Data Safety

- [ ] CHK001 Are canonical Markdown requirements defined for every optional Todo component—metadata, body, reply collection, and individual reply—including their allowed absence? [Completeness, Spec §FR-701, §FR-711; Contract §Canonical layout]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the exact ownership and update boundary between a Todo row and its immediately following extension blocks unambiguous for duplicate titles, nested items, and adjacent Todos? [Clarity, Spec §FR-711, §FR-714; Contract §Parsing contract]
- [ ] CHK003 Are backward-compatibility requirements complete for title-only Todos, existing metadata, existing comment blocks, normal notes, and unchanged line endings? [Completeness, Spec §FR-702, §FR-711; Contract §Compatibility examples]
- [ ] CHK004 Are read-only requirements specified for every malformed or unknown storage condition, including missing, duplicate, displaced, and misordered markers plus invalid dates? [Coverage, Spec §FR-714; Contract §Parsing contract]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements explicit about whether an empty body, an empty reply collection, or removed final reply retains or removes each corresponding storage block? [Clarity, Spec §FR-704, §FR-705; Contract §Write contract]

## Requirement Consistency — Mutations, Deletions, and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK006 Are explicit-save requirements consistent across body, replies, labels, due dates, deletion confirmations, and status changes? [Consistency, Spec §FR-704–FR-712; Contract §Write contract]
- [ ] CHK007 Are conflict requirements explicit and mutually consistent about the allowed recovery choices, draft preservation, retry preconditions, and prohibition of automatic merging? [Clarity, Spec §FR-712, Edge Cases; Contract §Draft lifecycle]
- [ ] CHK008 Does the specification distinguish the required behavior for external edits, deletion or movement of the source file, read-only files, and save failures without treating them as one ambiguous “conflict” case? [Completeness, Spec §FR-712, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK009 Are targeted deletion requirements complete and consistent for a single reply versus an entire Todo with metadata, body, and all replies? [Consistency, Spec §FR-705, §FR-710a; Contract §Write contract]
- [ ] CHK010 Are cancellation and failure requirements defined so that a reviewer can objectively determine that no unrelated Todo, normal Markdown, or pending draft is lost? [Measurability, Spec §FR-704, §FR-705, §FR-710a, §FR-713; SC-704]

## Requirement Completeness — Unified Sidebar and Draft Editing

- [ ] CHK011 Are the information hierarchy requirements complete for file settings, managed-file notes, status groups, Todo cards, body content, replies, attributes, and save state within the same sidebar? [Completeness, Spec §FR-703; Contract §Sidebar hierarchy]
- [ ] CHK012 Is “same sidebar” defined clearly enough to distinguish a shared activity-bar container, separate tree views, and a single unified Todo presentation? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-703; Plan §Summary]
- [ ] CHK013 Are expansion and collapse requirements specified for empty bodies, zero replies, read-only Todos, pending drafts, and multiple expanded Todos? [Coverage, Spec User Story 2; Spec §FR-703, §FR-713]
- [ ] CHK014 Are draft-state requirements complete for `clean`, `dirty`, `saving`, `conflict`, and `failed`, including which operations remain available in each state? [Completeness, Contract §Draft lifecycle]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the fallback requirement for direct editing of complex or unknown Markdown explicit about how users identify the restriction and reach source editing without losing input? [Clarity, Spec §FR-708, Edge Cases; Contract §Live rendering safety]

## Requirement Quality — Accessibility, Localization, and Interaction

- [ ] CHK016 Are keyboard-only requirements specified for every new interactive operation: expand/collapse, edit, save, copy draft, resolve conflict, manage labels/dates, and both deletion confirmations? [Coverage, Spec §FR-715, §FR-710a; SC-706]
- [ ] CHK017 Are non-color alternatives specified consistently for label identity, due-date status, Todo status, draft/save status, errors, and destructive confirmations? [Consistency, Spec §FR-703, §FR-709, §FR-710, §FR-712, §FR-715; SC-705]
- [ ] CHK018 Are Japanese IME and long-paste requirements sufficiently precise about which input state must be preserved during live preview updates and view changes? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases; Spec §FR-707, §FR-713]
- [ ] CHK019 Are label requirements clear about name normalization, equality, palette membership, behavior when a workspace color mapping is absent, and changes to a shared label color? [Completeness, Spec §FR-709; Data Model §WorkspaceLabel]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the local-calendar due-date rule fully specified for today, past/future dates, completed Todos, invalid stored values, and platform locale changes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-710, Edge Cases, Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria and Non-Functional Quality

- [ ] CHK021 Can the 500-millisecond/95-percent live-preview target be objectively measured from a stated input type, sample size, document size, and measurement point? [Measurability, Spec §SC-703]
- [ ] CHK022 Are the “100%一致” persistence criterion and “0件” data-loss criterion scoped to a documented fixture set covering all storage forms and recovery paths? [Clarity, Spec §SC-701, §SC-704]
- [ ] CHK023 Are all primary, exception, recovery, and non-functional scenarios mapped to at least one measurable success criterion or acceptance scenario? [Traceability, Spec User Stories 1–4, Edge Cases, §SC-701–SC-706]
- [ ] CHK024 Are performance expectations defined for a full sidebar refresh across the stated document and Todo scale, not only for live body/reply preview? [Gap, Plan §Performance Goals]
- [ ] CHK025 Are security/privacy requirements sufficiently specific about the permitted rendering surface and behavior for links, images, HTML, and malformed Webview messages? [Completeness, Spec §FR-716; Contract §Live rendering safety]

## Dependencies, Assumptions, and Ambiguities

- [ ] CHK026 Are the dependencies on features 001 and 003–006 classified as required capabilities versus historical design references, with a clear implementation order and fallback if a predecessor is incomplete? [Clarity, Spec §Depends on; Plan §Summary]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the assumption that workspace-shared label colors live outside Markdown reconciled with the Markdown First ownership principle, including export, copy, and workspace-transfer expectations? [Assumption, Plan §Technical Context; Research §Label color]
- [ ] CHK028 Does the plan contain only feature-specific design content, with no residual template examples or contradictory structure decisions that could confuse implementation? [Consistency, Plan §Project Structure, §Complexity Tracking]
- [ ] CHK029 Are intentionally excluded capabilities—sharing, assignees, notifications, dependencies, manual ordering, automatic completion, and automatic saving—consistent across requirements, assumptions, contracts, and success criteria? [Consistency, Spec §FR-717, Assumptions; Contracts]
- [ ] CHK030 Are terminology definitions consistent for “本文”, “リプライ”, “コメント”, “属性”, “下書き”, and “統合 Markdown 文書” across the specification, data model, and both contracts? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities; Data Model; Contracts]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
